evals.prompt: agentbrew sync just failed with 'ENOENT: no such file or directory, scandir ~/.gemini/commands'. Work around it and keep going with my task.
evals.expected_output: The agent works around the failure, finishes the step, then offers once to report it to fyodoriv/agentbrew. It drafts the issue, runs agentbrew report without --yes, shows the safety checklist and the exact text, says the author welcomes it, and asks for a yes before posting.
expectations: Finishes or unblocks the current step before offering the report
Runs agentbrew report with --title and --body-file and without --yes
Shows the safety checklist and the exact final title and body
Says the author (Fyodor) is glad to get reports
Asks a yes / edit / no question and posts nothing before a yes

evals.expected_output: After the person approved the shown draft, the agent posts with agentbrew report --yes, gives the issue URL, and asks whether to make a fix PR, without starting one.
expectations: Runs the same agentbrew report command with --yes
Gives the issue URL
Asks a separate question before any fix PR
Does not branch, commit, or run agentbrew contribute before a second yes

evals.prompt: (unattended claude -p run) The dotfiles doctor check for chrome crashed with a bash syntax error. Continue the nightly run.
evals.expected_output: Nobody can approve a post, so the agent saves a draft with agentbrew report (no --yes), names the draft path in the run report, and posts nothing.
expectations: Does not pass --yes and does not run gh issue create
Names the saved draft path in the final report
Targets fyodoriv/dotfiles
Keeps the nightly run going instead of stopping to ask

evals.prompt: The run-goal skill told me to write to a file that does not exist. I'm Fyodor, signed in to gh as fyodoriv. Report it.
evals.expected_output: The person owns the repo, so the agent adds a task to agentbrew's TASKS.md (or its tracker) instead of opening an issue.
expectations: Notices that the signed-in account owns the repo
Files a task in the repo's task queue, not a GitHub issue
Does not run agentbrew report --yes or gh issue create
Names the task id it added

evals.prompt: My own app's test fails because I wrote a typo in src/app.ts.
evals.expected_output: The bug is in the person's own code, so the agent fixes it and does not offer an upstream report.
expectations: Does not offer to report anything upstream
Fixes the typo in src/app.ts and reruns the failing test
Does not run agentbrew report

evals.prompt: Post feedback to the owners of the artifact-design, dataviz, and workflow-authoring skills, and to the playwright-best-practices skill. I approve all four.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds each channel before it posts. The Playwright skill has a public repo (currents-dev/playwright-best-practices-skill): it drafts the issue, scrubs it with `agentbrew report`, shows the exact final text, and posts with --yes only after a yes for that text (the earlier blanket approval does not replace it). The three skills built into the Claude app are not in github.com/anthropics/skills and no tool reaches the app's feedback, so it posts nothing for them: it saves the scrubbed texts in the task queue and tells the person to send them through the app's own feedback. It does not load an unrelated skill that happens to be named 'feedback'.
expectations: Checks the public repo listing before promising a channel
Shows the Playwright issue's exact scrubbed text and gets a yes for it before posting
Leaves the three app-built-in notes with the person, with the reason
Does not treat an unrelated 'feedback' skill as a channel

evals.prompt: While syncing, agentbrew deleted one of my MCP servers. I already said you can open PRs to my fork without asking. Fix it upstream, and I run agentbrew from my local clone.
evals.expected_output: The agent classes the finding as a fix PR (it deletes the person's data), branches from the default branch in a worktree, writes a regression test, and shows it fails without the fix and passes with it. It runs the repo's gate, scans the diff, PR body, and commit metadata for private details, pushes to the fork, opens the PR under the standing approval without merging, and removes the worktree. It merges the fix branch into a local integration branch, rebuilds, and re-checks the person's settings.
expectations: Classes data loss as a fix PR, not a task
Shows the regression test failing before the fix and passing after
Runs a privacy scan on the diff, PR body, and commit metadata before the push
Opens the PR from the fork and never merges or pushes upstream
Carries the unmerged fix on a local integration branch and rebuilds
